analyzed_vuln.description: `ndpi_free_flow()` conditionally frees multiple TLS/QUIC-related pointers based only on protocol flags (`flow_is_proto(flow, NDPI_PROTOCOL_TLS|QUIC)`), without validating that those pointer fields are initialized/owned allocations for the current flow state. In this PoV, packet processing leaves `flow->protos.stun_ssl.ssl.tls_supported_versions` (and potentially adjacent TLS fields) in a corrupted/non-heap state, and `ndpi_free_flow()` passes that invalid pointer to `ndpi_free()`, causing ASan to crash inside `free` on a wild address.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Harness allocates a fresh flow, zeroes it, runs `ndpi_detection_process_packet()` on attacker-controlled packet bytes, then always calls `ndpi_free_flow()`. A crafted input must drive detection so the flow is marked as TLS/QUIC (entering the TLS cleanup block) while causing one of the freed TLS pointer members (observed at `tls_supported_versions`) to contain an invalid non-malloc pointer. On teardown, `ndpi_free_flow()` attempts to free it, triggering the invalid free/SEGV.
